# Section 7 — One rule, many cars

<!-- GENERATED by logistics/scripts/stage_section_pages.py from sections/sec07/handout.md. Do not edit here; edit the section file. -->

*Groups of three, on paper. Agents are out for Parts A and B, in for Part C if you want them.*

$N$ cars on a ring of length $L$. Car $n$ sees only the gap $h_n$ to the car ahead and accelerates toward the speed that gap deserves (the *optimal-velocity* rule; Tuesday's notes wrote the stimulus as a speed difference with a reaction delay $T$; this rule reads the gap and relaxes toward $V$ at rate $a$, so $1/a$ is how long a driver lags behind the speed the gap deserves):

$$\dot x_n = v_n, \qquad \dot v_n = a\,\bigl(V(h_n) - v_n\bigr), \qquad V(h) \text{ increasing from } 0 \text{ to } v_{\max}.$$

### Part A — A different rule

Replace the rule by $\dot v_n = k\,(h_n - d_0)$: accelerate in proportion to how far the gap is from a preferred distance $d_0$.

1. What are the units of $k$ and of $a$? What does each measure about a driver?
2. Find the uniform steady state of the new rule: all gaps equal, all speeds equal. *(In the original rule the speed is $V(L/N)$. What fixes it here, and what condition on $L$, $N$ and $d_0$ does a steady state need?)*
3. Three cars on a ring, all at the preferred gap; car 1 brakes for one second. Sketch, without computing, what happens to the gap behind car 1, then to the next gap. Which way does the disturbance pass along the line of cars, toward the front or toward the rear?

### Part B — Two roads

Sixty cars, $L = 120$, the same tiny perturbation, two values of $a$. Position along the ring across, time up; color is speed along each car's path (dark is stopped).

```{figure} code/sec07/spacetime.png
:width: 82%
```
4. The drivers on one road respond faster (larger $a$) than on the other. Which road is which, and what on the picture tells you?
5. On the road with a jam: which way does the dark band move, and why does it move that way when every car moves the other way?
6. On the road without a jam, would adding more cars make it jam? ($V(h)$ is steepest at the spacing the cars already have.) One sentence, then name one change that *would* make it jam. *(AM215: name the one assertion a test of "uniform flow is a steady state" makes.)*

### Part C — If there is time: another crowd

Pick one: a flock of birds, people leaving a stadium, opinions in a group. Write the rule one individual follows (one sentence), the uniform state, and the one parameter that plays the role of $a$.
